newsitem.title: FRANCE: French train conductors vote on ending strike.
newsitem.headline: French train conductors vote on ending strike.

text.p: Some of France's striking train conductors began returning to work on Friday after union leaders made progress in all-night marathon talks with management on pay and conditions.
As conductors voted across the country on whether to end the three-day-old protest, the state railway company SNCF said there was a move towards returning to work.
It hoped to restore virtually normal traffic on all high-speed routes by 4 p.m. (1400 GMT) to try cope with a rush of travellers for the long Pentecost weekend.

The strike has cut services by about a third on high-speed TGV and regional lines across France, but has spared high-speed trains between Paris and Brussels and Eurostar trains connecting London to Paris and Brussels through the Channel tunnel.
"We obtained significant advances," said Bruno Dalberto, head of the pro-Socialist CFDT rail union after overnight talks ended at about 5 a.m. (0300 GMT).

Conductors were holding meetings around the country to vote on offers, ranging from higher bonuses to a plan to hire more staff. SNCF had said earlier it could not improve its terms because of financial constraints and the need to be fair to all staff.

Even if strikers agree to return to work, traffic would take several hours to return to normal, threatening misery for travellers leaving for the three-day Pentecost weekend. Trains cannot run without conductors, who are responsible for safety as well as checking tickets.
The conductors staged a similar strike last month in another sign of opposition to austerity policies of the centre-right government of Prime Minister Alain Juppe.
